subject: Architecture
title: Taipei 101: Beating the Wind and Quakes
description: A quick, practical guide to Taipei 101: Beating the Wind and Quakes.

hook.text: Taiwan faces typhoons and earthquakes. Building the world's tallest tower there seemed insane.

buildup.text: Taipei 101 rises 1,671 feet in one of the planet's most seismically active zones.

discovery.text: A 730-ton steel pendulum hangs near the top, swinging to counteract wind sway. Visitors can watch it move.

twist.text: The building survived a magnitude 6.8 earthquake during construction — a crane fell, but the structure held.

climax.text: Its bamboo-inspired segmented design isn't just decorative — each section resists wind independently.

punchline.text: Nature sends typhoons and earthquakes. Engineering sends them back.

quiz.question: What does the 730-ton pendulum inside Taipei 101 do?
options: Generates electricity from the building's movement
Swings to counteract wind sway and stabilize the tower
Anchors the building to bedrock during earthquakes
